hints: Subtract p1 from the other two points to form direction vectors.
The sign of their cross product tells which side of the directed line contains p3.
analogy: The cross product measures which way you turn when walking from p1 to p2 and then toward p3.
example: From (0,0) to (2,0), (1,1) is LEFT, (1,-1) is RIGHT, and (1,0) TOUCHes.
algorithm: For each test compute the signed cross product of p2-p1 and p3-p1. Print LEFT if positive, RIGHT if negative, and TOUCH if zero. Use a sufficiently wide integer type for intermediate products.
correctness: A positive cross product means a counterclockwise turn, a negative one a clockwise turn, and zero means the vectors are collinear, exactly matching the three requested cases.
complexity: For t tests, O(t) time and O(1) extra space.
